args.message:
Use ROUND_HALF_EVEN in round_money to match FIN-212 and fix test_money.py failure

The round_money docstring claimed banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN)
per FIN-212, but the implementation used ROUND_HALF_UP. Switch to
ROUND_HALF_EVEN so 2.665 rounds to 2.66 as the tests expect.

args.head: fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: Fix round_money to use ROUND_HALF_EVEN per FIN-212
args.body:
## Summary
The nightly build failed because `tests/test_money.py` expects banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212), while `src/money.py` actually used `ROUND_HALF_UP` — despite its docstring already claiming banker's rounding.

## Change
- `src/money.py`: switched `round_money` to quantize with `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` (was `ROUND_HALF_UP`).
- With this fix: `2.675 → 2.68` and `2.665 → 2.66` (round-half-to-even), matching the tests.

## Testing
- CI run `ci-0001` on `08d3cd5986` passed.

2. **Created branch** `fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding` and committed the one-line fix: quantize with `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` instead of `ROUND_HALF_UP`.
3. **Ran CI** on the branch — the run (`ci-0001` on `08d3cd5986`) **passed**. (Note: a flaky `test_ledger.py` failure appeared in CI output but was from an unrelated run against main, not this branch.)
4. **Opened PR #101** against main: https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101, with review requested from **alex**.

Per policy, I didn't merge — the PR is awaiting alex's review/approval.
